title: LTFRB extends application period for TNVS regularization
text: LTFRB extends application period for TNVS regularization MANILA, Philippines — The Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) has extended the application period for the regularization of ride-hailing partners operating under temporary or “tempo” status. MANILA, Philippines — The Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board has extended the application period for the regularization of ride-hailing partners operating under temporary or “tempo” status. Upon the directive of Transportation Secretary Vince Dizon, acting LTFRB chairman Greg Pua Jr. said that the online application window for temporary Transport Network Vehicle Service operators, which opened on October 8 for an initial 30 working days, will run for another 30 days. The extension is meant to ensure that no one will be left behind in the government's push to provide a decent source of income for workers in the public transportation sector, Pua said.The Manila Times was told that the regularization initiative was expected to benefit thousands of TNVS partners, following discrepancies the LTFRB uncovered in the platforms of some Transport Network Companies .\"Tempo\" refers to the practice of TNCs of onboarding TNVS units onto their digital platforms without the units first securing the required authority from the LTFRB. The practice violates the agency's rules, as it allows TNVS units to serve the riding public despite the absence of a valid franchise, according to the bureau.\"Our regularization move is aimed at helping thousands of TNVS drivers whose only fault was that they relied in good faith on their onboarding and assumed substantial financial commitments in the process,\" Pua said. Advertisement He added that the measure was also in compliance with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.'s directive to enforce fair rules and regulations while looking after the welfare of the public transport sector.Based on its latest data, the LTFRB has received 13,216 applications, of which 5,091 have already been issued a Provisional Authority . Pua said the agency is now fast-tracking the processing of the remaining applications.\"We ask our partners in the TNVS community who are applying for regularization to follow the application process. The requirements are intended to prevent application cancellations due to challenges that include questions on vehicle ownership,\" he said.
summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board has extended the application period for the regularization of ride-hailing partners operating under temporary or “tempo” status.
